title: Plugins
goal: Host CLAP on both targets and VST3 and AU through JUCE inside the graph, with latency compensation, state, capabilities and crash survival.
prerequisites: docs/harness/follow-ups.md, section Before M4: taken into the features below.

docs/harness/follow-ups.md, sections Before M4 wave 2: the graph driver's setBlocksComing is taken into m4-plugin-node; CLAP editor windows moved to Before M5 (decided by Fable, delegated by the maintainer, 2026-11-08).

humanGates.text: Choose the third-party plugins used for compatibility runs.
humanGates.how: The maintainer lists installed plugins; pluginval-checked runs use them.
humanGates.resolution: Decided by Fable, delegated by the maintainer, 2026-11-07. Windows compatibility set: TDR Nova, TDR VOS SlickEQ and Surge XT (VST3 and CLAP, the maintainer installs it) run on every maintainer run; Superior Drummer 3 (fallback EZdrummer 3), UAD 1176 and HALion Sonic run when authorised and SKIP otherwise, never prompting a login. Each takes one environment variable: SKIP when unset, FAIL when the path is missing. CI hosts only siann_test_plugin (VST3, CLAP, AU) and Apple AUPeakLimiter. macOS AU uses TDR Nova and Surge XT. Third-party LV2 waits for a Linux machine. MIDI output is proven on siann_test_plugin. SlickEQ's variable latency is unverified: if it is fixed, variable latency stays on siann_test_plugin.

features.title: CLAP host for both targets
acceptance: ClapPluginHost loads CLAP plugins in the desktop and headless builds; sample-accurate parameter events; latency and state through the PluginHost contract.

features.title: The engine process runs the graph driver on a device
acceptance: siann-engine builds a siann-playback graph from its session on a GraphDriver over the desktop JUCE output device (default, or --device <id> as siann-cli play takes it); the core-only build runs the same path on the fake device; transport.play {}, transport.stop {} and transport.locate {frames} are protocol methods; the realtime channel's playing flag and playhead come from the transport. Test: a client on the fake device plays, sees an advancing playhead in binary frames, locates and stops.

engine.status {} returns {device, playing, xruns, maxCallbackMicros, unmeasuredCallbacks, underruns, srcUnderruns} from the driver's CallbackTimer; a known miss driven through --fake-callback-nanos reaches a client (ADR-0018, condition 4). Without a device the engine still starts and serves; transport.play returns no_device.
Engine tests link siann_rt_alloc_guard; the restarted engine reopens the device, retrying under the shell's backoff.

features.title: Plugin slots in the document and PluginNode in the graph
acceptance: plugin.instantiate (a job that runs inside the request on the command thread) then plugin.insert (pure command) with a state blob, with the plugin_slot entity, Track.inserts, plugin.remove and plugin.set_bypass as the spec fixes them (siann-model, M4 plugin_slot; Commands and jobs, Jobs v0, plugins); missing plugins show as missing in engine.status with state preserved; instances survive unrelated edits through the pinned instance table.

PluginNode calls PluginInstance::process only from a GraphDriver callback or from the offline driver during bounce and export, never both at once; the driver's CallbackTimer covers the realtime path. Test: a hosted test plugin whose block exceeds its period counts as an xrun in the driver's timing (ADR-0018, condition 1).

The plugin event sink and the adapter's listener code only push to pluginEventAny (never setState, setParameter, device control or any wait for the audio thread: they run under JUCE's processMutex and listenerLock); the consumer of pluginEventAny runs on the command thread. Test: a plugin that reports from inside a restart and from the audio thread leaves the audio thread running (spec, "Threads and waiting rules"; ADR-0018, condition 2).
The adapter's triggerAsyncUpdate in audioProcessorChanged is replaced by an atomic tail-stale flag polled on the main thread, so no listener path can allocate.

MIDI output, decided 2026-11-08 (ADR-0018, condition 3; spec, Realtime rules and enforcement): JucePluginInstance preallocates its juce::MidiBuffer for Steinberg's 2048-event limit and counts, per instance, the blocks whose output exceeded it (midiOutputOverflows in engine.status), accepting JUCE's Array growth as plugin-caused; ClapPluginHost's bounded output list counts refused pushes the same way; the node drops the events after counting until MIDI tracks exist. Test: a plugin emitting more events than the preallocated size is measured and reported.

render.start keeps its snapshot semantics and instantiates its own instances on the command thread before the job is queued; the live graph never moves to the offline driver for it (spec, Commands and jobs, Jobs v0, plugins). Test: a test plugin counting concurrent process entries reports at most 1 while transport.play on the fake device overlaps render.start on the same document (ADR-0018, condition 1).

PluginNode times each PluginInstance::process into a per-instance CallbackTimer (atomics only), reported per instance in engine.status plugins[] (Protocol v0 item 18); a slow test plugin shows on its instance only.

A ctest check fails when SIANN code on the plugin process path (PluginNode::process, JucePluginInstance::process, event sink, listener adapter) names std::mutex, lock_guard, unique_lock, CriticalSection, ScopedLock, SpinLock or MessageManagerLock.

plugin.open_editor and plugin.close_editor (Protocol v0 item 19) replace the engine's --open-editor flag and the shell's SIANN_OPEN_EDITOR (spec, Process model); the launch tests and the human gates open an editor through the method; a CLAP plugin on the desktop target answers editor_failed until the Before M5 follow-up supplies a window.

The engine host's tick drains pluginEventAny as the spec's Threads and waiting rules say, and its instance table calls PluginInstance::setBlocksComing(true) when the driver's device starts, false after it stops, and true on an instance pinned while it runs (follow-up taken 2026-11-08). Test: a CLAP getState during playback on the fake device waits for a block and pauses nothing.

features.title: Hostile test plugin
acceptance: A built-in CLAP test plugin (siann_hostile_plugin) that allocates, throws, changes latency, sleeps and calls back into the host; the engine survives each behaviour with the documented outcome (spec, siann-host: two targets, one interface, Hostile test plugin).
The same plugin crashes the process on its crash parameter (std::abort, no dialog), reached through the live parameter path only and never from state.load, for m4-crash-recovery.

features.title: VST3 and AU through JUCE
acceptance: JucePluginHost formats behind the same PluginHost interface; capability flags exposed to agents through engine.capabilities.features.plugins {formats, flags}, the plugin.instantiate result and engine.status plugins[] (Protocol v0 items 14, 18 and 19); pluginval at strictness 5 runs on siann_test_plugin in CI and on the chosen plugins on maintainer runs.

The spec's audit of what JUCE runs inside processBlock (locks, and the allocation MIDI output can cause) is repeated for the JUCE pin in use before the pin moves; a lock or allocation the audit does not list reopens ADR-0018. LV2 through JUCE stays off (JUCE_PLUGINHOST_LV2=0): its wrapper takes a process-wide blocking SpinLock on the audio thread and grows a UI message buffer; LV2 arrives through lilv (M7) or worker processes.
A plugin exceeding maxPluginChannels (31; spec, PluginHost contract) fails with plugin_load_failed; test on a 32-channel siann_test_plugin layout.

features.title: Plugin crash recovery
specRefs: Two channels into the audio thread
acceptance: A plugin crash during playback leaves the UI alive; the engine restarts and recovers the session from checkpoint plus journal.

plugin.set_parameter {slotId, paramId, value} (Protocol v0 item 20; decided 2026-11-08): a live, non-journaled parameter path through the control dispatcher to the slot's PluginNode (CLAP as a parameter event in the next block; VST3 and AU through PluginControl::setParameter on the main thread), honouring expectedRevision and the idempotency cache, listed in engine.capabilities; not_found, plugin_missing and queue_full errors.

On Windows the engine's main() sets SetErrorMode(SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS | SEM_NOGPFAULTERRORBOX) and _set_abort_behavior(0, _WRITE_ABORT_MSG | _CALL_REPORTFAULT) before any plugin loads, so a plugin crash raises no dialog (spec, Process model, Crash).

Test: crash during transport.play on the fake device, triggered through plugin.set_parameter on the hostile plugin's crash parameter; the shell restarts the engine, session.sync returns the pre-crash revision id and documentHash, transport is stopped, and transport.play on the recovered session advances (the trigger was not durable). The deterministic core runs in the engine launch tests (a child engine that crashes, then a relaunch); the Playwright e2e proves the shell restart and the renderer staying connected; the CI app job builds the hostile plugin target and hands its path to the e2e through an environment variable.

exit.text: Third-party plugins load, save state, compensate latency and survive restart; capability flags are exposed to agents.
exit.how: Plugin tests plus pluginval runs on the chosen plugins.
